semantic_adjudication.reason: The NL2 contract requires the sub-machine to become active upon collision detection. The complete model inventory shows the collision event triggers the path DetectingState to junction1 (transition:line:22) and junction1 immediately routes to ActiveState (transition:line:23, untriggered, zero-time). The behavioral activation semantics of the NL are satisfied: when the collision event occurs, ActiveState is reached. The candidate imposes a structural requirement (a single direct edge with the trigger) that the NL text does not state. The NL says 'becomes active when... detected,' which is a temporal/behavioral condition on activation, not a mandate on transition graph topology.

This is a behavioral activation requirement, not a structural prescription for a single direct edge. The model satisfies this behaviorally: the collision event triggers transition:line:22 (DetectingState to junction1), followed by the zero-time untriggered transition:line:23 (junction1 to ActiveState). The observable consequence upon collision detection is that ActiveState is reached. The absence of a single direct structural edge does not defeat the NL's activation semantics.
